text:
Per-user chronological leave-one-out does not guarantee global temporal isolation: other users’ training interactions may occur after a validation event, inflating apparent forecasting ability. [A critical leakage study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.11060) documents this problem. Excluding future positives from a historical prefix’s negative pool uses hindsight to avoid false negatives; interpreting this as a prospective sampling policy would therefore be misleading. Distinguish exclusions based on later interactions already available within the permitted training split from exclusions requiring held-out labels. Never inspect hidden test interactions to construct exclusions.

Reusing training prefixes with targets already optimized during training measures fit and possible memorization, not held-out generalization. Conversely, a training history used to predict an unseen validation target is ordinary sequential evaluation. Candidate sampling also changes interpretation: [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show that sampled ranking metrics can reverse model rankings relative to full-catalog evaluation. Thus, HR@10 against 99 negatives supports conclusions about the pinned benchmark, without establishing equivalent full-catalog performance.

Suggested controls, keeping the evaluator unchanged: label prefix diagnostics explicitly as in-sample; compare training-prefix and validation performance; stratify existing validation outcomes by training-only target popularity, history length, and repeated-item status; measure recommendation popularity and catalog coverage on permitted histories. History-order shuffling and history truncation can probe dependence on sequence information, though neither alone proves memorization. Popularity deserves scrutiny because offline data can reward reproducing exposure bias ([Castells and Moffat](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/aaai.12051)). Keep these descriptive diagnostics separate from selection: retain macro validation HR@10 and one trained NextItNet checkpoint per category, with no auxiliary score fusion.
